Tests of the provider effects of a discrete-time fixed-effect fit

Source: R/test_discrete_fe.R
test.discrete_fe.Rd

Tests \(H_0: \gamma_i = \gamma_0\) for every provider (or a subset) with the score or the Wald statistic and a model-based or clustered variance, and flags the providers above or below the null value.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'discrete_fe'
test(
  fit,
  statistic = c("score", "wald"),
  variance = c("naive", "robust"),
  null = "median",
  providers = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  wald_variance = c("case_mix", "full"),
  null_model = NULL,
  interval = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted by fit_discrete_fe().

statistic

"score" (default) or "wald".

variance

"naive" (default; model-based) or "robust" (sandwich clustered by patient, or by subject when pp_data() has no patient column).

null

the null value \(\gamma_0\): "median" (default) or "mean" (weighted by person-periods) of the fitted effects, or a number.

providers

optional subset of provider identifiers to report.

level

confidence level; the significance level is 1 - level.

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

wald_variance

for statistic = "wald" with the naive variance: "case_mix" (default) or "full", see gamma_variance().

null_model

optional null model, as in test.logistic_fe(); the result is then passed through calibrate().

interval

for the score statistic, compute the confidence limits of \(\gamma_i\) by inverting the test (default TRUE).

...

unused.

Value

A data frame of class pp_test, with the columns of test.logistic_fe().

Details

With \(H_j(g) = \sum_{k \le t_j} \mathrm{expit}(g + \hat\alpha_k + Z_j^\top\hat\beta)\) the expected events of subject \(j\) over its periods at risk and \(W_j(g)\) the sum of \(h(1 - h)\):

  • score: \((O_i - \sum_{j \in i} H_j(\gamma_0)) / \sqrt{V_i}\) with the naive \(V_i = \sum_{j \in i} W_j(\gamma_0)\) or the clustered \(V_i = \sum_c (\sum_{j \in c} \delta_j - H_j(\gamma_0))^2\);

  • Wald: \((\hat\gamma_i - \gamma_0)/se\), with the variance of gamma_variance() or the clustered standard error \(\sqrt{V_i} / \sum_{j \in i} W_j(\hat\gamma_i)\).

These are the statistics of test.logistic_fe() on the person-period data. The exact and likelihood-ratio statistics are not offered: a subject leaves at its event, so a provider's event count is not a sum of independent trials. Under the model the person-periods of a subject are uncorrelated, so there is no stabilized variance.

The limits of the score statistic invert the test as in test.logistic_fe(); a provider with no events has no finite lower limit.

Examples

s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, provider_size = c(20, 40), rows_per_patient = c(1, 1),
              type = "survival", seed = 1)
s$month <- pmin(ceiling(s$stop * 12), 12)
s$event[s$stop * 12 > 12] <- 0
pd <- pp_data(s, x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider", patient = "patient",
              time = "month", event = "event", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_discrete_fe(pd)
test(fit)
#> Provider tests: score statistic, naive variance (modified); null median = -3.013; two.sided, level 0.95
#>   20 providers: 3 above, 1 below, 16 not different, 0 not tested
#>  provider estimate se null_value statistic       p flag  lower  upper observed

#>      P002   -3.885 NA     -3.013   -1.7819 0.07477    0 -4.840 -2.931        4
#>      P003   -2.535 NA     -3.013    1.5398 0.12362    0 -3.140 -1.931       11
#>      P004   -2.601 NA     -3.013    1.1993 0.23043    0 -3.266 -1.936        9
#>      P005   -3.713 NA     -3.013   -1.7256 0.08442    0 -4.503 -2.922        6
#>      P006   -3.640 NA     -3.013   -1.6634 0.09624    0 -4.376 -2.905        7
#>  expected variance
#>    10.666    9.948
#>     9.299    8.845
#>     7.016    6.695
#>     6.108    5.814
#>    11.758   11.134
#>    12.791   12.123
#>   ... 14 more rows
test(fit, statistic = "wald", variance = "robust")
